captions.caption: A close-up view shows wood shavings and sticks prepared for a fire between two logs.
The camera pans across various sizes of sticks laid out for a "long fire" setup.
The flashlight illuminates the different bundles of kindling arranged on the dark ground.
The camera moves to show the progression from thin wood shavings to thicker sticks.
A person's hand is seen briefly as they show the fire preparation in the dark.
The setup features two parallel logs that will serve as the base for the fire.
The light focuses on the smallest kindling, which is mostly thin twigs and wood shavings.
The camera continues to pan, highlighting the organized rows of wood categorized by size.
The person explains the fire setup while showing the various stages of fuel prepared.
A wider shot displays the two logs with the fire materials nestled between them.
The flashlight beam sweeps over the ground and the prepared logs in the dark woods.
The camera shows the rear log, which is part of the long fire structure.
A small metal container is seen sitting on one of the logs in the darkness.
The camera pans back to the central area where the fire will be ignited.
Further inspection of the firewood preparation is conducted by the person at night.
The person adjusts the camera angle to better show the entire fire layout.
The light moves across the logs, showing their length and parallel placement.
A view of the sticks arranged by size, ready to be added once the fire starts.
The camera focuses on the wood shavings, which are the primary tinder for the fire.
The person prepares to start the fire, with the camera showing the complete setup.
A brief moment of stillness occurs before the fire-starting process begins.
The flashlight illuminates the dark forest floor around the prepared fire pit area.
The person moves into position and prepares to strike a ferro rod for ignition.
The person holds a ferro rod and a knife, getting ready to create sparks.
The person strikes the ferro rod for the first time, producing initial bright sparks.
Multiple sparks are produced as the person vigorously strikes the ferro rod with a knife.
The person continues to strike the rod, aiming the sparks at the wood shavings.
Sparks fall onto the tinder, but a flame has not yet caught on the shavings.
The person adjusts their grip and position for a more effective strike on the ferro rod.
A sequence of bright sparks illuminates the immediate area around the tinder pile.
The person focuses their strikes on a specific spot within the wood shavings.
More sparks are directed into the center of the tinder pile to ignite an ember.
The person strikes again, and a small ember begins to glow within the shavings.
A large burst of sparks successfully ignites the wood shavings into a small flame.
A small, bright flame appears and begins to consume the center of the tinder.
The flame grows slightly as it spreads through the fine wood shavings.
The person puts away the ferro rod and prepares to add more fuel to the fire.
The person carefully places additional wood shavings onto the growing flame.
Smoke starts to rise from the small fire as it begins to catch more fuel.
The person uses their hands to shelter the small flame from any potential breeze.
The person adds a few small twigs to the flame to build up the heat.
The flame is now stable and starting to spread through the initial tinder.
More thin sticks are added to the fire to ensure it stays lit and grows.
The person gently blows on the base of the fire to provide it with more oxygen.
The fire brightens significantly as the small twigs catch and begin to burn.
The person continues to carefully manage and feed the young fire between the logs.
A clear flame is visible, casting light onto the surrounding logs and forest floor.
The person adds slightly larger pieces of kindling to the center of the fire.
The fire is now strong enough to burn steadily without constant manual attention.
The person begins to arrange the kindling to create a sustainable bed of coals.
The person reaches for a handful of small branches to add to the growing fire.
The branches are placed over the flames, which quickly begin to consume them.
The fire grows taller, illuminating the person's hands and the base logs.
The person mentions the time, noting that it is about twenty minutes past seven.
More dry leaves and small sticks are added to increase the intensity of the fire.
Thick white smoke rises as the newly added fuel starts to catch fire.
The person adjusts the position of the wood to better contain the flames.
The fire is now well-established and providing a significant amount of light.
The person continues to add wood, moving from smaller kindling to larger pieces.
The fire crackles as it burns through the pile of wood between the two logs.
